p01.why: An array of unknown bound has the alignment of its element type.

p02.why: The operand of sizeof has the incomplete type Inc; only decltype allows a call with an incomplete return type.

p03.why: A dynamic_cast to a derived reference checks at run time and can throw, and a cast to a pointer cannot.

p04.why: alignof needs a complete type, and Inc is incomplete.

p05.why: Negating an unsigned value gives 2^N minus the value, so -0u is 0 and -1u is the largest value.

p06.why: A built-in addition and a call to a noexcept function cannot throw; a call to a function without noexcept and a throw can.

p07.why: The operand of sizeof must not have a function type.

p08.why: The operand of prefix ++ must not be bool.

p10.why: --i on the smallest int overflows during constant evaluation.

p11.why: The temporary's destructor is called implicitly: Risky's can throw and Calm's cannot, so both assertions hold and main returns 0.

p12.why: *p is x as an lvalue, and &*p gives p back.

p13.why: With -m32 a pointer and the type of sizeof 0 are 4 bytes on Clang and GCC; EDG skips -m32 tests.

p14.why: The operand of * must be a pointer.

p15.why: Prefix ++ and -- step ints, doubles, and pointers by one, and ++(++i) works because ++i is an lvalue.

p16.why: The operand of alignof must not be void.

p17.why: The operand of unary - must not be a pointer.

p18.why: alignof takes a type; Clang and GCC accept an expression only as an extension that -pedantic-errors rejects.

p19.why: lowest is the smallest int, so its negation overflows, and UBSan stops the run.

p20.why: int(C{}) calls a conversion function without noexcept, and D's conversion function is noexcept.

p21.why: The operand of prefix ++ must not be const.

p22.why: sizeof of a parameter declared as an array gets a -Wsizeof-array-argument warning on Clang and GCC, and -Werror makes the warning an error; EDG skips -Werror tests.

p23.why: The default allocation function is not noexcept.

p24.why: A pointer operand must point to a complete object type.

p25.why: A cast to a reference to an accessible unambiguous base or to the operand's own class makes no check, so each noexcept is true; main returns 0.

p26.why: On x86-64 a pointer and the type of sizeof 0 are 8 bytes.

p27.why: The operand of prefix -- must not be bool.

p28.why: A short at its largest value stepped by ++: Clang and GCC convert the value back to -32768, EDG rejects (Q-0124).

p29.why: a is a reference to an array, so sizeof gives the array size with no warning; EDG skips -Werror tests.

p30.why: The type that p points to can be incomplete, and binding a reference does not read the object.

p31.why: *p reads through a null pointer, and UBSan stops the run.

p32.why: Dereferencing a null pointer during constant evaluation is undefined.

p33.why: The result of prefix ++ is the operand as an lvalue, so decltype gives int&.

p34.why: Unsigned values wrap, and unsigned char steps in int then converts back to 0.

p35.why: The operand of prefix ++ must not have an enumeration type.

p36.why: The character types have size 1, an array has the size of its elements, and a reference gives the size of the referenced type.

p37.why: *(a + 2) reads through a past-the-end pointer during constant evaluation.

p38.why: 42 is a prvalue, so & cannot take its address.

p39.why: The operand of alignof must not be a function type; the extension is rejected under -pedantic-errors.

p40.why: ++n on the largest int overflows, and UBSan stops the run.

p41.why: A pointer to a function is not a pointer to a complete object type.

p42.why: The copy reads an object of incomplete type through *p.

p43.why: char has alignment 1, alignments are powers of two, and arrays and references take the element or referenced type's alignment.

p44.why: & on an lvalue gives a pointer to its type with the same cv-qualifiers, also for arrays and functions.

p45.why: Moving a pointer two past the end during constant evaluation: GCC accepts, Clang and EDG reject (Q-0031).

p46.why: true is promoted to int 1, so -true is the int -1.

p47.why: The operand of sizeof is not evaluated, so i stays 0.

p48.why: ++i on the largest int overflows during constant evaluation.

p49.why: & on a qualified member name gives a pointer to member.

p50.why: An empty class has size at least 1, and a class's size includes its members and padding.

p51.why: A signed char at -128 stepped by --: Clang and GCC convert -129 back to 127, EDG rejects (Q-0124).

p52.why: The operand of unary - must not have a scoped enumeration type.

p53.why: *f gives the function, which converts back to a pointer for the second *, so both calls return 1.

p54.why: T's constructor is not noexcept and N's is.

p55.why: noexcept does not evaluate its operand, so calls stays 0, and count is not noexcept.

p56.why: The operand of * must not be a pointer to void.

p57.why: The operand of sizeof must not be void.

p59.why: nullptr has type std::nullptr_t, which is not a pointer.

p60.why: The operand is promoted, so char, short, and enumerator give int, unsigned stays unsigned, and an array becomes a pointer.

p62.why: A function operand of unary + becomes a pointer to the function.

p63.why: The global allocation functions are not noexcept and the deallocation functions are; main returns 0.

p64.why: A member call through a null pointer during constant evaluation: Clang and GCC reject, EDG accepts (Q-0318).

p65.why: A member call through a null pointer is undefined, and UBSan stops the run.

p66.why: Unsigned values wrap, and the postfix forms give the old value.

p67.why: == calls an operator function without noexcept, and != is a rewritten comparison that calls the same function; main returns 0.

p68.why: Negating the smallest int overflows during constant evaluation.
